verses.author: model_A
verses.text: My grandmother's hands remember a language I never learned.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
flour and water still know
the shape her palms gave them—
some words don't need a mouth

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the dough rises anyway
under the same window light
where no one is speaking

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
steam fogs the glass
until the window forgets
it was ever a mirror

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the mirror's forgetting
teaches my hands something
her mouth never had to say

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
what her mouth never said
still shapes the bread I break—
crumbs falling like small answers

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
small answers scatter on the table
where I sweep them into my palm
and eat what silence taught me

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
what silence taught me
I feed to the sparrows now
they ask nothing back

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
they ask nothing back
so I keep the last crumb hidden
for a hunger that has no bird

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a hunger that has no bird
still comes to the window at dusk
and I open it anyway

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
I open it anyway
though nothing flies in but the cold
and I call that company too

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I call that company too
so I set two cups on the table
and drink from whichever one is warm

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
steam rising off whichever one I choose
I name it patience
though it is only waiting with a better face

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the kettle keeps its own counsel
so I stand here learning
how long steam takes to mean nothing

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the window fogs where I breathed on it
a small gray country
gone before I could live there

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I wipe the glass clean with my sleeve
and there's the yard again, unmoved
waiting the way things wait when they don't need me
